text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a confident assessment of the group's operating position, senior executives at National Mutual Holdings, Australia's second-largest life office, yesterday indicated that most divisions were performing strongly, saying the group is on target to beat its $210 million maiden profit as a publicly listed company. Page 1.

South Australian mortgage broker Growden Finance Group, which has a half-share of the market in South Australia, with more than 1,000 investors, is in the hands of receivers after the Australian Securities Commission asked the Federal Court to protect investors due to concerns about the way the business was being run. Page 4.

Due to concerns arising from recent drilling results about the depth of Helix Resources NL's Tunkillia gold discovery in South Australia and the possibility it may be a low-grade body of less than one gram a tonne, investors slashed A$65 million off the junior gold explorer's market capitalisation yesterday. Page 17.

John Faraci, the chief executive of Carter Holt Harvey Ltd, which last year bought Forwood Products from the South Australian Government for A$130 million, revealed yesterday the company intends to increase its Australian timber and forests investments despite severe price pressures that contributed to a sharp fall in earnings in the first nine months of the year. Page 17.

Following a decision on Monday by Ausdoc Group directors to flatly reject a A$114 million, A$2-per-share takeover offer from Brambles Industries Ltd, Brambles yesterday gave up hope of snaring services company Ausdoc, saying it will not increase its offer which falls well short of the valuation contained in a Grant Samuels & Associates independent report. Page 17.

Following a decision by National Foods Ltd to sell its packaging arm NationalPak, analyst Stella Shao, of credit rating agency Standard & Poor's Australia, revealed yesterday the agency has revised down its outlook for National Foods to negative from stable, but has reaffirmed its "BBB" rating for the company. Page 19.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Addressing National Mutual Holdings Ltd's subdued and brief inaugural annual meeting in Melbourne yesterday, where he unexpectedly announced his impending retirement, outgoing chairman Athol Lapthorne told shareholders performance in the December quarter was encouraging and said the group was on target to better last year's maiden profit. Page 21.

In a result which is bad news for Acacia Resources Ltd, which last Friday spent A$38 million buying 17.4 per cent of Helix Resources NL, recent drilling results from Helix, the star of the Gawler Craton in South Australia, have proved to be disappointing and investors have responded by sending the share price plunging by 25.5 per cent. Page 21.

Seven Aboriginal native title claimants to the A$1.1 billion Century Zinc project in the Queensland Gulf are today expected to decide whether to adopt a draft agreement, which was placed together after intensive talks throughout the Gulf region over the past month, that could clear the way for development of the world-class zinc mine. Page 21.

Due to a sharp contraction in lending margins coupled with a lower fee income, the Bank of Melbourne posted a surprise two per cent drop in interim profits. The profit downturn comes just two weeks after the departure of the bank's highly regarded former chief executive, David Airey, and reflects the bank's high exposure to the home lending market. Page 21.

National Foods Ltd credit outlook was downgraded from stable to negative by ratings agency Standard and Poor's because of its A$206 million sale of its most profitable NationalPak division. National Foods' actual BBB rating was unchanged at one level above the lowest cut-off for investment grade, with the maintenance of the grading being dependant on cash-flow generation and improved margins. Page 23.

An increased takeover bid of A$2.25 a share for Perth-based Mt Edon Gold Mines NL from Canadian-based Teck Corp and local miner Camelot Resources NL was accepted by Mt Edon directors. The directors recommended shareholders accept the offer after earlier rejecting a A$2.15 a share offer. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Answering questions following an address to the Sydney Institute, Reserve Bank Governor Ian Macfarlane said a further cut to official interest rates was possible if the ACTU's "living wage claim" and future enterprise bargaining agreements did not blow out wage growth figures. Page 29.

Bureau of Statistics figures released yesterday indicate lower interest rates are enticing home-buyers into the market, with housing finance approvals rising 5.3 per cent in December, in seasonally adjusted terms. However, builders and suppliers say the flow-on benefits are still some way off. Page 29.

National Mutual Holdings managing director Geoff Tomlinson said healthy investment markets, sound trading in the domestic market and a booming share price for subsidiary National Mutual Asia pointed to significantly improved profits this year. Page 29.

The failure of Helix Resources to provide further evidence that it was tracking a major gold system in South Australia's Gawler Craton triggered the market to yesterday wipe nearly A$100 million from the value of exploration companies in that region. Pae 29.

National Association of Retail Grocers of Australia president Ian Baldock said small retailers are unfairly carrying the burden of the bank's encouragement of electronic banking channel use. Baldock said banks were abdicating their responsibilities by inceasing fees and shoving costs to retailers. Page 31.

Bank of Melbourne reported its December half profit had fallen 2 per cent from A$41.0 million to A$40.1 million, 6.4 per cent lower than the six months to June 30. The Bank's first profit fall since 1992 was attributed to fierce competition on home lending and interest rate pressure. Page 31.
THE AGE

Suffering its third blow in as many weeks, Bank of Melbourne Ltd announced a A$40.1 million bottom line for the half-year to December - two per cent down on the same period last year and 6.4 per cent lower than for the six months to June 1996. The result s BoM's first profit fall since 1992 and comes despite speculation that a takeover bid is imminent. Page C1.

In response to Gawler Craton high-flyer Helix Resources release late on Monday of poorer than expected results from the third line of drill holes on Area 223 at Tunkillia, Helix shares plunged A$1.32 yesterday to A$3.67 a share and its recently arrived major shareholder, Acacia Resources, was pushed 11 cents lower to A$2.06 on its A$38 million investment. Page C1.

National Mutual Holdings managing director Geoff Tomlinson says NM was looking to Thailand and China as its big expansion hopes after projecting a significant boost in profits at the annual meeting. NM is waiting for a Thai license application to be processed with retiring chairman Athol Lapthorne telling shareholders that winning a license in China was a top priority. Page C3.

Loscam half-year report, released yesterday, revealed company directors have decided not to pay a dividend, with funds being directed to cutting debt instead. Loscam reported net profits of A$1.4 million for the half year, coinciding with a A$54.2 million takeover bid by General Electric's G.E. Capital Services Unit. Page C3.

National Foods' has been slammed by the credit rating agency Standard & Poor's for its decision to sell its most profitable business, NationalPak. S & P downgraded NatFoods' outlook to negative, claiming the sale had weakened the group's overall business profile. Page C3.

Mining contractor and civil engineer Henry Walker Group has increased its interim dividend on a December-half profit that rose from A$9.45 million to A$10.81 million. Revenue in the first-half soared from A$200 million to a record A$258.1 million as demand for contract services boomed. Page C3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
